name: Probability & Statistics
description: Probability axioms, conditional probability, random variables, standard distributions and basic statistics for GATE.

nodes.name: Probability basics
nodes.desc: Sample spaces, events, the axioms, complements and the addition rule, with dice, coins and cards.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define sample spaces and events and compute probabilities with the axioms, complements and the addition rule.

nodes.name: Counting & probability
nodes.desc: Equally likely outcomes counted with permutations and combinations: birthday, urn and sampling-without-replacement problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute probabilities of equally likely outcomes using permutations and combinations in classic counting problems.

nodes.name: Conditional prob.
nodes.desc: P(A|B), the multiplication rule and sequential experiments.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute conditional probabilities and use the multiplication rule for sequential experiments.
topics: Conditioning as reducing the sample space

nodes.name: Independence
nodes.desc: Independent events, pairwise versus mutual independence, and repeated trials.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test events for independence and distinguish pairwise from mutual independence in repeated trials.

nodes.name: Total probability
nodes.desc: Partitioning the sample space and the law of total probability.
nodes.summary: You will be able to partition a sample space and compute probabilities with the law of total probability.

nodes.name: Bayes' theorem
nodes.desc: Inverting conditional probabilities with Bayes' theorem; priors, likelihoods and posteriors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to invert conditional probabilities with Bayes' theorem and interpret priors, likelihoods and posteriors.

nodes.name: Random variables
nodes.desc: Discrete and continuous random variables, PMF, PDF and CDF.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe discrete and continuous random variables with PMFs, PDFs and CDFs.

nodes.name: Expectation & variance
nodes.desc: Expectation, linearity, indicator variables, variance and standard deviation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute expectations and variances, using linearity and indicator variables to simplify hard problems.

nodes.name: Joint distributions
nodes.desc: Joint and marginal distributions, sums, minimum and maximum of random variables, conditional expectation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to work with joint and marginal distributions, sums, minima and maxima of random variables and conditional expectation.

nodes.name: Discrete distributions
nodes.desc: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric and Poisson distributions: their means, variances and when to use each.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose among Bernoulli, binomial, geometric and Poisson distributions and use their means and variances.

nodes.name: Normal & exponential
nodes.desc: Uniform, exponential and normal distributions, memorylessness and standardising.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use uniform, exponential and normal distributions, apply memorylessness and standardise normal variables.

nodes.name: Limit theorems
nodes.desc: The law of large numbers and the central limit theorem, and the normal approximation to the binomial.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the law of large numbers and central limit theorem, including the normal approximation to the binomial.

nodes.name: Markov chains
nodes.desc: States, transition matrices, stationary distributions and simple random walks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model systems as Markov chains with transition matrices and find stationary distributions.

nodes.name: Descriptive statistics
nodes.desc: Mean, median, mode, variance and standard deviation of data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to summarise a data set with measures of centre and spread such as mean, median, mode and standard deviation.

nodes.name: Correlation
nodes.desc: Covariance, the correlation coefficient and the Cauchy–Schwarz bound.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute covariance and the correlation coefficient and explain why correlation always lies between -1 and 1.

nodes.name: Statistical inference
nodes.desc: Sampling distributions, estimators, confidence intervals and the idea of hypothesis testing (t, chi-square).
nodes.summary: You will understand sampling distributions and estimators and be able to build confidence intervals and outline t and chi-square tests.

nodes.name: Hypothesis testing
nodes.desc: Null and alternative hypotheses, p-values, z and t tests, and type I and II errors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up hypotheses, compute z and t test statistics and p-values and interpret type I and II errors.
topics: Type I and type II errors

nodes.name: Least-squares line
nodes.desc: Fitting a line to data by least squares and reading the correlation coefficient.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fit a least-squares line to data and interpret its slope together with the correlation coefficient.
